header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Rates are from enrolled SB 392 (2026), which cut every rate about 5% retroactive to 2026-01-01: 2.11% to $10,000, 2.81% to $25,000, 3.16% to $40,000, 4.22% to $60,000, 4.58% above (Tax Foundation's January 2026 table and the Tax Division's undated IT-140ES instructions still show older rates: 2.22%-4.82% / 2.36%-5.12%). Single, MFJ and HOH share one schedule (no doubling for joint filers); MFS uses half-width brackets ($5,000 / $12,500 / $20,000 / $30,000). No standard deduction. Personal exemption $2,000 per exemption including dependents ($500 if zero exemptions). Social Security: 100% of federally taxable benefits are subtracted for all taxpayers beginning tax year 2026. Senior modification: taxpayers 65+ (or permanently disabled) may subtract up to $8,000 of income from ANY source, but it is reduced by other decreasing modifications claimed, including the Social Security and public-pension modifications (taxpayer effectively gets the greater), so retirees with $8,000+ of taxable Social Security get no additional benefit. Separate modifications exist for certain public, military and public-safety pensions (not modeled). Municipal service fees excluded.

flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: 8,000 at 65+ applies to income of any kind and is reduced dollar-for-dollar by the Social Security and public-pension modifications claimed
